segments.text: American Fork City Council — Regular Session — June 9, 2020:

City Administrator David Bunker said American Fork contributed more than legally required toward public-safety retirement benefits and explained that employees would pay the remaining 0.27%. He also said movement from Tier 1 to the less costly Tier 2 system would offset some future costs.

Council Member Barnes asked about the projected $7,000 annual budget impact of the public-safety retirement contribution and whether costs would rise as additional employees moved from Tier 1 to Tier 2.
The council discussed the city’s retirement contribution for public-safety employees and the budget effect of employees moving between retirement tiers.
Relevant discussion from the official meeting minutes:

Mr. Bunker said that the City’s Public Safety employees were grateful to the Council for the contributions. The City contributes more than is legally required. He clarified that the remaining .27% would be required by the employee, but American Fork continues to be generous to their Public Safety employees.

Council Member Barnes commented on the budget impact of $7,000 annually as outlined in the packet. He noted that as they move forward, and more people transition from being tier one to tier two he that the budget impact would continue to rise. Mr. Bunker said that Council Member Barnes was correct. However, as more people became tier two, less people were on tier one which was a higher contribution and cost the City more. Because of this, the transition to tier two was actually beneficial to the City.
